Use the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √D) / (2a). If D = 0, one real root. If D < 0, complex roots. Always verify solutions by substituting back into the original equation.

Differentiate y = f(x) to get f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points. Substitute each x-value into f(x) to find the corresponding y-values.
